direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels like a very raw and gritty, intimate portrait into the lives of inmates in the prison system, using its indie feel to show the harsh realities of the environment meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law; The direction on a microscale is meant to make you empathize with the main character as you see what he is going through, his addiction, his hope to get out and see his son, and how all of this might be taken away from him after Dee gets introduced into his life; The storytelling is good and clear as it's easy to follow and uses your emotional investment in the main character to keep you engaged; They use tension incredibly well to keep you on the edge of your seat, despite how hard it is to watch at times, as it accurately shows the lawlessness of the prison environment despite it being a place meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law

performance.comments: Is the emotioanal core of the movie as the whole story flows through his performance; he shows the toll that prison life and addiction takes on a person, as he uses the latter to deal with the stresses of the former; has a really good dynamic with Blyth, as they play off each other really well; there is one monologue/conversation though that I felt was a bit unnatural and takes a step down in the performance
Steals the show in his scenes as he is a big personality that tries to make sure he is the biggest person in the room; has a really good dynamic with Jonsson as they play off each other really well

cast.comments: Uses a combination of actors and former inmates to help show the harsh realities of prision life as they create a lawless environment despite being in a place meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law;

story.comments: The concept is an intimate portrait into the life of an inmate/addict; The plot structure is linear and easy to follow; Character writing is good as the main character is well-written and keeps you invested in his story, with the whole movie being an intimate portrait into his life as an inmate and an addict, where the latter is used to deal with the harsh realities of being the former

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is strong and helps build the world of the prison environment; The humor is good and makes the movie enjoyable; The symbolism is strong as the movie shows the lawlessness of the prison environment despite it being a place meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law; The movie also shows how many turn to drugs and addiction to deal with the harsh realities of being an inmate; The foreshadowing is good, especially with the ending, as even though it does make the movie a bit predictable, it creates a satisfying ending

score.comments: Tonally really fits the movie as it helps give the film a very British underground feel and does an amazing job of building tension

soundtrack.comments: Helps give this movie a very British underground feel

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is raw, gritty, and 'in your face,' successfully giving the film an indie feel that serves as an intimate portrait into the life of an inmate, as well as an addict; The use of vertical phone footage adds to this realism, as many times it is this type of footage that we see in documentaries about prison life (like the Alabama Solution); The film also uses the camera as somewhat of a character, with the characters spitting blood into the lens, which further highlights the lawlessness of the prison environment; Being so up close and personal also shows the claustrophobia of prison life as this helps build tension to create breaking points for many inmates

editing.comments: Works in conjunction with the cinematography to create a raw, gritty, indie feel, while still highlighting some of the beauty in the shots

visual_effects.comments: Uses a lot of practical effects as the movie is very much an indie film, but it uses them well and shows you don't need a big budget to make a film that keeps you invested

production_design.comments: Builds the prison environment accurately as it shows how caged in and confined the prisoners are, and how this creates a lawless environment despite being in a place meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law

makeup.comments: Shows the blood and gore of the prison environment, showing the harsh reality of a lawless prison environment meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law; Paints the tattoos on the actors to help show the world these characters live in

review.pacing: Pacing is right as the movie is only 90 minutes and doesn't feel too long or too short
review.climax: Climax is incredibly tense and honestly so hard to watch because of how emotionally invested you get with the main character and his journey; The ending is the right ending, even though it is a bit predictable
review.tone: Tone is very British underground, with its style, tone, and music as this indie movie feels like a raw and gritty portrait of the life of an inmate/addict
review.final_notes: Received a screener and reviewing for Creators Choice Awards
review.overall: Overall, 'Wasteman' is an intimate portrait into the raw, gritty life of an inmate and addict, showing how many turn to the latter to deal with the harsh realities of the former as the film shows how the prison system creates a lawless environment despite it being a place meant to contain and 'rehabilitate' those who break the law; the film is able to accomplish this through its cinematography, direction, writing, and performances as all of these elements work in conjunction to create a realistic experience that makes you emotionally invested in the main character and his journey to turn his life around, despite how external forces are setting him up to fail
